thread:
emma: Heads-up — experiment results from last night's bid-hysteresis + latency-aware hedge run.
raj: nice, high level? :eyes:
miguel: Short version: price-optimized pools cut avg cost by ~18% but we saw p99 jumps when spot churned. capacity-optimized stable but ~6% more expensive.
emma: Exactly. The hysteresis tweak (don't switch bids until price crosses threshold for 3m) reduced oscillation, but latency-sensitive routes still suffered during mass evictions.
kai: Do you have eviction counts / timeseries? we need to see alignment with our warmbuffer TTLs.
miguel: eviction spike at 03:14–03:22 UTC, ~22% of spot nodes in us-west1 went. oncall-bot reported surge.
oncall-bot: alert: spot-eviction-rate spike detected 2026-03-11T03:14Z, rate=0.22, affected_pool=price-optimized-us-west1
raj: Oof. How did that affect in-flight requests? tail latency impact?
miguel: p50 ~ unchanged, p95 +30ms, p99 +120–160ms for inference_small routes.
emma: Proposal: mix pools per region with a small capacity-optimized warm buffer and a dynamic hedging weight that shifts to capacity-optimized when eviction rate > 8% for 10m.
raj: Sounds reasonable. How big should warm buffer be?
emma: Start with 6% of steady-state GPU nodes in each region for latency-sensitive namespaces. Keep TTL=15m for warm replacements, pre-warm images.
kai: I want a safety valve: if evacuation rate > 25% or queue backlog > 1000, failover to dedicated fallback cluster (dedicated-us-west1).
miguel: We ran a sim: mixed pool with 6% warmbuffer + hysteresis reduced p99 regressions by ~65% during the same eviction event, cost delta +3.2% vs pure price-optimized.
raj: That's a good tradeoff. Can you paste the config snippet you used for the sim?
miguel: Sure:
```
hedge_policy:
  target_mix:
    price_optimized: 0.80
    capacity_optimized: 0.14
    warmbuffer: 0.06
  hysteresis_seconds: 180
  eviction_trigger_pct: 0.08
  failover_threshold_pct: 0.25
warmbuffer:
  ttl_minutes: 15
  prewarm_image: "redwood/inference:v5-prewarm"
  labels: ["latency-sensitive"]
```
emma: Ops checklist before rollout:
- add telemetry for eviction-to-latency correlation (per-region)
- tune warmbuffer autoscale step to avoid thrashing
- add per-namespace override so gen-model jobs can stay price-optimized
- run 48h canary in us-west1 with synthetic traffic
kai: Also add egress / cross-region capacity guardrails — we saw some replicas tried to reconstruct in secondary region and caused bandwidth spikes.
raj: Good call. How do we coordinate cost center approval? finance needs the +3.2% delta explained.
emma: I'll draft a short note highlighting reduction in p99 regressions and expected cost delta, include the sim charts. pinging @raj for numbers to attach.
miguel: One more note: set lower bid_floor for capacity-optimized pools to avoid bidding up in scarce auctions — we used 60% of on-demand as floor in sim.
raj: LGTM. Rollout plan:
1) telemetry + alerts (48h)
2) canary config in us-west1 (48h synthetic)
3) expand to eu-west2 and us-east1 (staggered)
4) review cost after 2 weeks
emma: I'll open the rollout PR after I add dashboards. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
kai: +1
oncall-bot: notify: schedule follow-up meeting Tue 09:30 UTC to review canary metrics.
